title: TTL propagation lag triggered cross-region escalation postmortem
creator: Ava Tran
description: On 2026-03-01 a ~40m window of amplified fallback traffic occurred when regional routing entries expired out-of-order due to a TTL propagation lag in the control plane. The incident caused higher-cost tier escalations and increased latency for affected customers in EU-West and APAC. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-01T09:15:00Z - On-call triage: observed increasing percent of traffic routed to higher tier variants and cross-region fallbacks. Dashboards show EU-West node eviction churn.
2026-03-01T09:24:00Z - Initial mitigation: temporarily increased routing-entry TTLs (control plane flag) to reduce churn while investigate. Partial stabilization observed.
2026-03-01T09:40:00Z - Identified correlation between control-plane write batching and delayed tombstone propagation to edge routing caches.
2026-03-01T10:05:00Z - Rolled back a config change to control-plane GC that had been deployed 2026-02-28 (gc-window reduction).

2026-03-01T10:30:00Z - Full mitigation: re-enabled per-region heartbeat backpressure and deployed a hotfix that multiplexes eviction notifications to caches. Traffic returned to expected routing ratios by 10:47Z.
impact_summary: Approximately 12k requests/min were routed to fallback variants across EU-West and APAC for ~40 minutes. Average 95th percentile latency increased by 120ms for impacted routes and token spend on higher-cost variants increased by an estimated 18% for the window. No customer data was exposed; errors were within RTO limits but cost and latency SLOs were impacted.
root_cause: A recent optimization to control-plane tombstone GC (reduction of gc-window to improve memory usage) inadvertently changed the batching semantics for eviction notifications. Under normal load this produced small propagation delays; under the regional rolling restart that was happening concurrently, propagation lag exceeded routing cache TTLs causing some edge caches to observe stale routing entries and trigger cross-region fallbacks. In short: control-plane TTL/GC semantics + concurrent rollout caused out-of-order expiry at the edges.
technical_findings: Control-plane change (PR #5731) reduced tombstone GC window from 120s to 30s to reclaim memory; this altered the batching code path for eviction events.

Eviction notifications are multiplexed and de-duplicated in the control plane; reduced window increased the chance of a notification being dropped from the immediate delivery path and queued in a lower-priority batcher.

Edge routing caches use a soft TTL (routing_entry_ttl) of 45s; they accept tombstones but also rely on heartbeat-driven revalidation. When tombstones arrive late, caches did not revalidate quickly enough and continued to route to drained nodes or variant mappings that no longer matched capacity.

During a concurrent regional rolling restart in EU-West, node heartbeat gaps were frequent and amplified the effect of late tombstones, producing cascading fallback amplification into Dedicated/high-tier variants in other regions.
Alerting gap: no metric tracked 'eviction-notification-latency' end-to-end; existing alerts focused on control-plane error rates and edge cache miss ratios which trailed the root cause.
Regression test coverage did not simulate concurrent GC tuning + rolling restarts across many regions.
mitigations: Hotfix rolled: restored gc-window to 120s and updated the eviction batcher to guarantee synchronous delivery for high-priority tombstones (deployed 2026-03-01 10:30Z).
Increased default routing_entry_ttl from 45s to 90s to provide extra hysteresis for delivery jitter while we implement more robust guarantees.
Emergency runbook step added: during regional rolling restarts, disable aggressive GC or flip routing-entry TTL to emergency-high to avoid simultaneously exposing caches to late tombstones.
Adjusted monitoring: added 'eviction_notification_latency_ms' and an alert when 95th percentile > 500ms for any region.
long_term_actions: Replace soft TTL based cache expiry with lease-based routing entries where control plane issues a short-lived lease token and edges must revalidate before switching variants. Owner: @marcus; ETA: 2026-04-15.
Implement end-to-end tracing for eviction events (control-plane -> distribution -> edge cache) to surface propagation delays in dashboards. Owner: @sophia; ETA: 2026-04-01.

Add a canary test that simulates concurrent GC tuning + region rolling restart and measures routing stability and fallback amplification. Integrate into pre-release gating for control-plane changes. Owner: @eng-reliability; ETA: 2026-03-25.
Introduce automatic rollback policy in the deployment pipeline when 'eviction_notification_latency_ms' alert triggers during a rollout. Owner: @ci-cd; ETA: 2026-04-05.

Rework routing fallback policy to prefer in-region cheaper variants unless explicit capacity shortage; reduce cross-region escalation sensitivity by increasing hysteresis and adding per-route cost budget checks. Owner: @policy-team; ETA: 2026-04-22.
Run a post-deployment audit of the recent control-plane tuning PRs and add a checklist item ensuring TTL semantics are preserved. Owner: @review-board; ETA: 2026-03-18.
Security review not required for these changes; KMS/HSM unaffected.
testing_and_validation: Load test: replayed 1.2x production routing churn while injecting tombstone delays; new batcher guarantees prevented cross-region fallbacks in repeated runs.
Canary: hotfix rolled to a single EU-West cluster for 2h, monitored eviction_notification_latency_ms and top-5 route fallback ratios before wider rollout.
Smoke: validated that routing_entry_ttl increase did not materially affect time-to-drain for dedicated capacity by running 50 drain scenarios and ensuring no increase in queue backlog beyond 3%.
postmortem_notes: Decision rationale: raising routing_entry_ttl is a tactical, short-term mitigation to buy time for a lease-based design. TTL increases carry risk (longer time to drain) but we judged the cost/latency impact acceptable compared to cascading cross-region escalations.

Trade-offs discussed in review: synchronous tombstone delivery adds extra control-plane latency under heavy churn; we mitigated by making only high-priority tombstones synchronous and leaving best-effort for low-impact events.
Customer comms: drafted a short write-up for affected accounts summarizing impact and mitigations; customer success to reach out to top 12 affected customers. Owner: @cs-tilly.
